ticket.title: Ticket
ticket.summary: Unified inbound customer matter — request, complaint or contactmoment
ticket.description: The ticket supertype folds the former request, complaint and contactmoment schemas into one object distinguished by a ticketType discriminator (unify-ticket-supertype). A ticket is any inbound customer matter: a request/demand (with pipeline & queue), a complaint/klacht (with SLA & resolution) or a contactmoment (a single logged interaction, optionally hanging off a parent request-ticket). Per-type Schema.org identity is preserved via x-schema-org-by-type.

x-openregister-archival._note: unify-ticket-supertype: the retired `contactmoment` schema carried a VNG/AVG retention policy (default P2Y, plus outcome rules). `request` and `complaint` carried NONE. A merged schema can hold only ONE archival block, and the condition DSL supports a single comparison (no AND), so the two postures are reconciled with ordered, first-match-wins rules: the two ticketType rules below exempt request/complaint tickets (P100Y == effectively never disposed, matching their previous no-retention behaviour), and everything after them applies only to contactmoment tickets, whose original default (P2Y) is preserved below. CONSEQUENCE: OpenRegister's SCHEMA_ARCHIVAL_IMMUTABLE guard is schema-level, so tickets can no longer be hard-deleted by hand — they expire via ArchivalRetentionTask. That is the intended posture for an auditable client-interaction record, but it IS a change for request/complaint tickets.

rules.reason: Request-type tickets carried no retention policy before the ticket merge; exempted here so the merge does not start auto-disposing them. Revisit with the DPO if requests should acquire a real retention term.
Complaint-type tickets carried no retention policy before the ticket merge; exempted here so the merge does not start auto-disposing them. Klacht retention is a separate DPO decision.

Resolved client contact moments (callback logs, counter/phone interactions) retained 2 years as the operational client-interaction record (VNG Klantinteracties), then disposed per ADR-024. DPO sign-off pending (task 4.1).
Transferred (doorverbonden) contact moments are short-lived routing records; 1-year retention before disposition. DPO sign-off pending.

start.description: Pick up the ticket for handling. Authorization: the assignee or a member of the sales group.

complete.description: Resolve a request-type ticket successfully. Authorization: the assignee (per-object owner RBAC).

convert.description: Convert a request-type ticket into a case (Procest). Authorization: the assignee (per-object owner RBAC).

resolve.description: Resolve a complaint-type ticket to the customer's satisfaction. Authorization: the assignee (per-object owner RBAC).

reject.description: Reject the ticket as unfounded or out of scope. Authorization: the assignee or a member of the sales group.

close.description: Close a contactmoment-type ticket (interaction logged, no further action). Authorization: the assignee (per-object owner RBAC).

x-openregister-handoff._note: Moved from the legacy `request` schema. Request-type tickets convert into a Procest case; the handoff is offered on the ticket surface and the source template keeps the `pipelinq:request:` prefix so already-converted cases still resolve.

ticketType.title: Ticket Type
ticketType.description: Discriminator: request (demand/case), complaint (klacht) or contactmoment (logged interaction). Deliberately has NO default: it is `required`, so any create path that forgets to set it fails validation loudly rather than silently filing a complaint or contactmoment as a request. TicketService::save() always stamps it; manifest form dialogs render it as a required choice.

title.title: Title
title.description: Ticket headline. For a contactmoment this is the interaction subject.

description.title: Description
description.description: Full description. For a contactmoment this is the interaction summary.

client.title: Client
client.description: UUID reference to the associated client.

contact.title: Contact
contact.description: UUID reference to the associated contact person.

assignee.title: Assignee
assignee.description: Nextcloud UID (or agent) handling the ticket.

status.title: Status
status.description: Unified lifecycle status across all ticket types.

channel.title: Channel
channel.description: Intake/interaction channel. Free string spanning all type vocabularies (phone/email/web/counter/letter for request+complaint; telefoon/email/balie/chat/social/brief/sms for contactmoment).

occurredAt.title: Occurred At
occurredAt.description: When the matter was raised (request.requestedAt) or the interaction happened (contactmoment.contactedAt).

parentTicket.title: Parent Ticket
parentTicket.description: For a contactmoment: UUID of the parent request-ticket this interaction belongs to (migrated from contactmoment.request).

category.title: Category
category.description: Free-text request category for classification (request only).

pipeline.title: Pipeline
pipeline.description: UUID reference to the pipeline this request is tracked in (request only).

stageOrder.title: Stage Order
stageOrder.description: Ordinal of the current pipeline stage (request only).

queue.title: Queue
queue.description: UUID reference to the routing queue (request only).

caseReference.title: Case Reference
caseReference.description: UUID of the Procest case this request converted into (request only).

complaintCategory.title: Complaint Category
complaintCategory.description: Classification of a complaint-type ticket (migrated from complaint.category).

resolvedAt.title: Resolved At
resolvedAt.description: When the complaint was resolved (complaint only).

duration.title: Duration
duration.description: Interaction duration (ISO-8601 duration or free string) (contactmoment only).

channelMetadata.title: Channel Metadata
channelMetadata.description: Channel-specific metadata envelope, e.g. call duration, email thread id, chat transcript link (contactmoment only).

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Free-text notes on the interaction (contactmoment only).
